slides.heading: Compare Leaf Traversal
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Compare Leaf Traversal, a very hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Do two trees have the same sequence of leaves left-to-right?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Do two trees have the same sequence of leaves left-to-right? Lazy iterators.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Walk both trees' leaves lazily in parallel so we can stop at the first difference.
slides.narration: Walk both trees' leaves lazily in parallel so we can stop at the first difference.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Collect both leaf lists, compare → O(n + m) space
Lazy stacks → O(h1 + h2) space, early exit
slides.narration: Collecting both leaf lists works but uses linear space. Lazy generation with stacks uses only height space and can stop early.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Iterator per tree with a stack
slides.narration: Step by step. First, iterator per tree with a stack. Second, advance to the next leaf. Third, compare values. Fourth, both must end together.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Compare leaves left to right
slides.narration: Two trees match if their leaves, read left to right, are the same sequence.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: two stacks: pop until a leaf; push right then left
compare one leaf at a time

slides.caption: Generate leaves lazily with stacks
slides.narration: Use one stack per tree to produce the next leaf on demand, and compare leaf by leaf, stopping at the first mismatch.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: All equal → true
slides.narration: All four leaves match, and both run out together, so it's true.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Next leaf pops nodes, pushing right then left children, until it pops a leaf. The main loop compares leaves until either runs out, returning true only if both run out together.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n plus m. Space is O of h1 plus h2.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Push right before left so leaves come out left to right.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Point out the early exit on mismatch.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Walk both trees' leaves lazily in parallel so we can stop at the first difference.
slides.narration: To recap Compare Leaf Traversal: Walk both trees' leaves lazily in parallel so we can stop at the first difference. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
